items.text: Voted to leave public health coverage for older residents intact: the budget law cut none of that coverage's benefits for citizens. In the existing system, public health coverage is guaranteed only to older, disabled, and low-income residents, and about 8 percent of residents have no coverage.

Abstained on the chamber's first passage of a budget bill that reduced funding for public health coverage for low-income residents, added work requirements to that coverage, and reduced food assistance, then voted for the final version.
Cosponsored a bill to phase down over eight years the higher national funding share for adults added to low-income public health coverage until it equals the regular share.
Voted against a three-year extension of expanded premium subsidies for individually purchased health insurance.
Voted for a bill that loosened rules for employer and association health plans and did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
Voted for a funding bill that did not extend the expiring premium subsidies.
As head of a group of legislators, warned party leaders that the group's members would withhold their votes from any funding bill carrying an extension of the expanded premium subsidies.

After the budget law passed, said its work requirements and its limits on the financing arrangements regional governments use would discourage further expansion of public health coverage for low-income residents.
